reason: This passage from 2 Samuel 11-12 contains multiple regular human characters with direct speech, emotional expression, and stated opinions. David displays anger (וַיִּֽחַר־ אַף דָּוִד - 'David's anger was kindled greatly'), Bathsheba mourns (וַתִּסְפֹּד עַל־ בַּעְלָהּ - 'she mourned for her husband'), Uriah speaks and expresses his principle about not abandoning the army (הָאָרוֹן וְיִשְׂרָאֵל וִיהוּדָה יֹשְׁבִים בַּסֻּכּוֹת...), David's servants voice opinions questioning his behavior, and Nathan the prophet delivers pointed judgments. These characters are not mere functionaries but have substantive dialogue, emotional arcs, and moral positions they articulate.
